title: PrePay Power (Prepaid Metering) Training Note: Overbilled Share After a Fast Meter Test
content:
**Rule.** For a PrePay Power (Prepaid Metering) meter error refund, where an earlier meter test of the same service account found the meter within tolerance before the fast test with an error on the fast side, the error is taken to have grown between the two tests and the overbilled share is the average of the earlier error and the error found divided by one hundred plus that average; where there is no such earlier fast-side reading and the error found is below twice the meter accuracy tolerance, the overbilled share is the error found less the tolerance, divided by one hundred plus that difference; a test in any other situation keeps the error found over one hundred plus that error.

The readings come from the meter tests of the service account in its Electric Service by Rate Schedule records: the error percentage recorded on the fast test, and on the most recent test that found the meter within tolerance. An error on the fast side is a recorded error above zero. The tolerance is the meter accuracy tolerance of the underlying rate schedule. The share itself is not rounded.

### Questions answered (hypothetical readings)

**The earlier within-tolerance test read 1.2 percent fast and the fast test found 3.4 percent.** The average is 2.3, so the share is 2.3 divided by 102.3.

**The earlier within-tolerance test read 0.5 percent slow (an error below zero); the tolerance is 2.0 and the fast test found 3.4.** The earlier reading is not on the fast side. Twice the tolerance is 4.0 and 3.4 is below it, so the share is 1.4 divided by 101.4.

**No earlier within-tolerance test; tolerance 2.0; error found 4.0.** 4.0 is not below twice the tolerance, so the share is 4.0 divided by 104.0.

**Same, error found 3.9.** Below 4.0: the share is 1.9 divided by 101.9.

**The within-tolerance test came after the fast test.** It is not before the fast test, so it is not an earlier fast-side reading for this rule.
